correctness.rationale: For every unselected edge uv, perfect edge domination is exactly deg_F(u)+deg_F(v)=1. The F-zero-degree vertex set U must be independent; every edge with both ends outside U is in F, so F=E(G[V\U]). For K_{m,n} minus t distinct matched edges, any independent U is confined to a single side or one missing pair, and the deg_F=1 condition allows only stars centered on unmatched vertices, except K3,3 minus its whole matching, which is C6 with three 2-edge and six 4-edge choices. Hence for 3<=m<=n,0<=t<=m the polynomial is (n-t)z^m+(m-t)z^n+z^(mn-t), except (3,3,3) with 3z²+6z⁴+z⁶. Independently enumerated 2,228,672 exact edge subsets for 22 parameter triples, confirming every polynomial; for n>=4 deleting the last matching edge changes two n-edge minima into a unique n(n-1)-edge minimum.
